# PDTF 2.0 — Property Data Trust Framework

> The Property Data Trust Framework version 2.0 replaces OpenID Connect verified claims with W3C Verifiable Credentials, decomposes the monolithic property data schema into an entity graph, and introduces decentralised identifiers and cryptographic signing.

## Overview
- Website: https://pdtf2.propdata.org.uk/
- GitHub: https://github.com/property-data-standards-co
- Author: Ed Molyneux / Moverly

## Key Concepts
- Entity Graph: Transaction, Property, Title, Person, Organisation, plus role-embodying relationship credentials SellerCapacity, Offer, Gift, Representation, TransactionRole
- Credentials: W3C Verifiable Credentials v2.0 data model, secured as SD-JWT-VC with mdoc at the GOV.UK identity boundary (provisional, 02 §2.4, consultation Q20); the reference libraries currently implement Data Integrity (eddsa-jcs-2022, Ed25519)
- Identity: did:key (persons; did:key or did:web for organisations), did:web (transactions, adapters), urn:pdtf:* (properties, titles, relationships, credential ids)
- Trust: OpenID Federation 1.0, Trust Anchor https://propdata.org.uk (interim; governance consultation Q6), trust marks pdtf-verified-issuer / account-provider / regulated-conveyancer (provisional, Q7) with entity:path delegation; trust levels root_issuer, trusted_proxy, account_provider, assertion
- Revocation: IETF Token Status List (`status` claim; provisional, follows Q20, 14 §1); W3C Bitstring Status List in the Data Integrity representation the libraries implement
- Three trust phases: Moverly trusted proxies → hosted adapters → primary source root issuers

## Implementation
- [@pdtf/core](https://github.com/property-data-standards-co/core) — signing, verification, DIDs, status lists, TIR client
- [OpenID Federation](https://github.com/property-data-standards-co/tir) — live registry data
- [Schemas](https://github.com/property-data-standards-co/schemas) — JSON Schemas

## Consensus Questions
17 open questions (Q1.1–Q6.3) requiring industry consensus, documented in the Architecture Overview §14.
